\begin{proof}
Since $x^3-9$ has degree $3$, it is reducible over $\mathbb{F}_{31}$ if and only if it has a root. Suppose that $a^3=9$ for some $a\in\mathbb{F}_{31}$. Then $a\ne0$, so Fermat's theorem gives $a^{30}=1$. Consequently,
\[
9^{10}=(a^3)^{10}=a^{30}=1.
\]
But direct modular computation yields
\[
9^{10}\equiv5\pmod{31},
\]
which is not $1$. This contradiction shows that $x^3-9$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_{31}$. Hence it is irreducible.
\end{proof}

outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
A polynomial of degree $3$ over a field is reducible precisely when it has a linear factor, equivalently a root. We show that $x^3-9$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_{31}$. If $a^3=9$ with $a\in\mathbb{F}_{31}$, then $a\ne0$ and
\[
9^{10}=a^{30}=1
\]
by Fermat's theorem. On the other hand,
\[
9^2\equiv19,
\qquad 9^4\equiv19^2\equiv20,
\qquad 9^5\equiv20\cdot9\equiv25,
\]
so
\[
9^{10}\equiv25^2\equiv5\not\equiv1\pmod{31}.
\]
Therefore $9$ is not a cube in $\mathbb{F}_{31}$, and $x^3-9$ has no root. Thus $x^3-9$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{F}_{31}$.
\end{proof}
